title: Raised lower bounds for 34 square counts, including s(114) ≥ 87/8 = 10.875 (follow-up to #1039)

labels.name: intake
labels.description: Tracking intake (saving, validation, tabulation, credits) of new results

body:
[squaremath_continued_20261119.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/35084690/squaremath_continued_20261119.zip)

**Credit name.** Joost de Winter, Delft University of Technology, after Hiroaki Hosono.

**Claim.** Lower bounds for 34 square counts between 50 and 137, each a direct certificate with its own complete coverage check. The largest increase is at 114, from 10.807801610697 (#1039) to 87/8 = 10.875. The case page lists the upper bound 11 there, so the gap shrinks from 0.19 to 0.125. Every bound is an exact rational, listed in `lower_bounds.csv` and in the table below.

**Certificate.** Attached file `squaremath_continued_20261119.zip`, SHA-256 `d8d0d6966f7ac7f9a69f24d578619ee2323a158e5c6c9c7e6be9039c401445df`. Comparisons use jlevy/squares at `1015fc175fa4e2c01f912d915d784100e36d3bab` and the bounds submitted in #1039.

**Argument.** Each certificate places a nonnegative rectangle measure on the board of the claimed side, with total mass strictly below the square count. The checker proves that every unit square in the board, at every orientation and centre, captures mass at least one. For an angle interval with half-width σ around orientation θ₀, the octagon |u| + σ|v| ≤ 1/2, |v| + σ|u| ≤ 1/2 lies in every unit square of that interval, and the checker moves this octagon through all permitted centres with integer area bounds. Square boundaries carry no mass, so a packing would need more mass than the measure holds. Details are in `proof/INTEGER_CHECKER.md`.

**Constructions.** The measures come from Hosono's measures and from the reweighted measures of #1039. Two steps are new. A strip step repeats the central unit strip of a measure on each axis, which raises the board side by two (the 73-square measure at 8.826 gives a 114-square measure at 10.826). A mixture step combines measures transplanted from several counts with integer weights. The bound at 114 mixes measures from 92, 93 and 74 squares with weights 9184590 : 73911664 : 16903746. All mixtures and weights are listed in `constructions/README.md` and rebuilt with rational arithmetic.

**Checking.** Run `python3 verify.py` (Python 3.10+, C++17 compiler with 128-bit integers). It checks all input hashes, rebuilds every measure, and checks the recorded coverage of all angle intervals. `python3 verify.py --replay --workers 4` repeats every centre subdivision, with negative controls at quarter-strength weights. `python3 verify.py --n 114 --replay --workers 4` replays the bound at 114 alone (100 angle intervals, 1,406,930 centre boxes). Both the full check and the replay at 114 passed on a separate machine.

**Not claimed here.** The packet also holds 67 bounds from new corner measures (`corners/`) that inherit the global coverage of Hosono's T-180 measures without replaying it, and a packing of 260 squares that differs from earlier certificates by 1.6e-15. This issue claims neither.

**Lineage and AI assistance.** Hiroaki Hosono constructed the source measures. The reweighted measures and the integer checker come from my earlier submissions, #1039 and T-327. OpenAI GPT-6.2 Astra carried out the numerical search, the derivations and the certificate construction under my direction.
